reports.verdict: Shopify held 32% revenue growth while profits jumped faster, with operating income up 66%, and guided to a similar low-thirties pace next quarter.

takeaways.label: Profit outgrowing sales
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 66% to $568 million, and free cash flow margin hit 22% versus 18% a year ago. Losses on payments and loans fell to $120 million from $148 million.

takeaways.label: Growth steady, not accelerating
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 32%, down from 34% last quarter and in line with the low-thirties guide. Sales volume on the platform rose 29% to $119 billion.

takeaways.label: Q4 outlook: profit-per-sale squeeze
takeaways.text: Q4 revenue is guided to low-thirties growth, but gross profit only high-twenties, so profit per sales dollar thins. Expenses are guided to 29-30% of revenue.

takeaways.label: Big buyback begins
takeaways.text: Shopify repurchased $562 million of its own stock in the quarter, with none a year earlier. R&D spending rose 33% to $497 million.

reports.verdict: Teva raised 2026 sales guidance again as brand drugs grew 33%, but profit guidance barely moved and generics keep shrinking.

takeaways.label: Brand drugs accelerate
takeaways.text: Austedo ($751M, +21%), Ajovy ($269M, +61%) and Uzedy ($85M, +96%) together hit about $1.1B, up 33%. Forecasts for all three were raised again.

takeaways.label: Sales outlook up, profit flat
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue guidance rose to $16.7–17.0B from $16.5–16.85B. Adjusted EPS guidance stayed essentially unchanged at $1.92–2.11, and the top end of operating income and EBITDA ranges was cut.

takeaways.label: Generics a drag
takeaways.text: Total revenue fell 2% to $4.4B as generics sales dropped 16%, mainly from lower sales of the cancer drug generic lenalidomide. Profit margins still improved.

takeaways.label: Balance sheet turns corner
takeaways.text: Moody's and S&P upgraded Teva to investment grade after Fitch. About $4.9B of debt was refinanced; debt is $16.7B, with a goal of reaching 2x leverage by end of 2027.

reports.verdict: Marathon Petroleum earned a record $26.93 per share as refining margins soared, then raised its dividend 10% and added a $5 billion buyback.

takeaways.label: Record refining profit
takeaways.text: Adjusted profit was $26.93 a share, up from $3.01 a year earlier. Refining margin hit $45.70 a barrel versus $17.60, with refineries running at 100% capacity.

takeaways.label: Bigger shareholder payouts
takeaways.text: Marathon returned $3.3 billion in the quarter, raised its dividend 10% and added a $5 billion buyback, bringing total buyback room to $8.1 billion.

takeaways.label: Selling two refineries
takeaways.text: Marathon will sell its St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries and related pipelines for $4.2 billion, with $3.45 billion going to Marathon. Closing is expected at year-end, with proceeds to be reinvested mainly on the Gulf Coast.

takeaways.label: Pipeline arm growing
takeaways.text: Its pipeline partner MPLX raised its payout 12.5%, which should send Marathon about $3.1 billion a year. Cash stands at $13.6 billion.

reports.verdict: Pfizer raised its 2026 outlook as cancer and heart drugs offset collapsing COVID sales, but Eliquis pricing and falling vaccine sales cloud the picture.

takeaways.label: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: Full-year revenue outlook rises $1.5B at the midpoint to $62-64B. Adjusted EPS outlook rises to $2.95-$3.05 from $2.80-$3.00, despite a one-time $0.10 licensing charge.

takeaways.label: Growth drivers vs COVID
takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $16.6B. Excluding COVID products, sales grew 7%, and recently launched and acquired drugs grew 32%. Padcev rose 55% and Lorbrena 43%. Paxlovid fell 63%.

takeaways.label: Eliquis boost is partly pricing
takeaways.text: Eliquis sales rose 25% to a $513M gain, driven mainly by lower rebates and favorable channel mix in the U.S., a less repeatable source than rising demand.

takeaways.label: Vaccines weakening
takeaways.text: Prevnar fell 10% on lower U.S. vaccination rates and lost adult market share. Comirnaty fell 29% on narrower U.S. recommendations. Adjusted EPS of $0.87 was flat year over year.

reports.verdict: Apple beat on sales and profit, but guided December-quarter margins down to 45%–46% as record memory-chip costs cut into profit.

takeaways.label: Margin squeeze
takeaways.text: December gross margin is guided to 45%–46%, below the 47.9% just reported (about 1 point of which was one-time tariff refunds) and under the 46.3% analysts expected. Memory costs drive most of the drop.

takeaways.label: Record holiday growth
takeaways.text: Apple guided December-quarter revenue up 7%–10%, above the 6.1% analysts expected, and called it the best quarter in company history. It gave no outlook beyond December.

takeaways.label: Supply limits demand
takeaways.text: The new iPhone Duo is supply-constrained and Apple can't say when supply will meet demand. Mac and iPad supply will also be tight in December because of memory.

takeaways.label: Costs and softer spots
takeaways.text: Spending on AI-driven R&D is guided up 11%–13%. Services growth slows to 8%–9%, Greater China revenue of $17.5 billion missed estimates, and iPad and wearables fell.

reports.verdict: Revenue nearly doubled and U.S. business customers now outspend the U.S. government, but new-deal growth slowed sharply to 6%.

takeaways.label: Commercial overtakes government
takeaways.text: U.S. commercial revenue rose 148% to $984M, passing U.S. government revenue ($953M) for the first time. Total revenue rose 96% to $2.31B versus about $2.18B expected.

takeaways.label: Forecast raised again
takeaways.text: Full-year revenue guidance rose to about $8.53B (91% growth) from about $8.15B, versus roughly $8.2B expected. The Q4 forecast is about $2.65B, and profit margins stay near 62%.

takeaways.label: New deals lag revenue
takeaways.text: New contract value signed was up only 6% to $2.9B, and U.S. commercial signings rose 11%. Revenue is growing far faster than new bookings.

takeaways.label: International commercial stalls
takeaways.text: International commercial revenue grew 21% year over year but only about 1% from the prior quarter. Management gave no figures on Europe, and Germany's military is evaluating 30 AI tools.

reports.verdict: Refining windfall and a $20 billion 2027 buyback plan lifted shares.

reasons.label: Big refining rebound
reasons.text: Fuel-making profit more than doubled to $9.1 billion from $4.1 billion last quarter.

reasons.label: Huge 2027 buyback
reasons.text: Plans $20 billion of share repurchases in 2027, after $5.1 billion bought this quarter.

reasons.label: Strong cash, less debt
reasons.text: Free cash flow was $19.1 billion, and net debt fell by nearly $11 billion this year.

reports.verdict: Refining-driven profit beat expectations, lifting shares modestly despite lower production and oil prices.

reasons.label: Refining profits surged
reasons.text: Fuel margins pushed refining earnings to $4.9 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier.

reasons.label: Beat on estimates
reasons.text: Adjusted EPS of $5.28 topped the roughly $4.89 analyst average.

reasons.label: Cash and debt gains
reasons.text: Free cash flow near $14.2 billion; net debt fell to $20.7 billion from $34.5 billion.

reports.verdict: Revenue beat estimates and AbbVie raised its outlook again, lifting the stock modestly.

reasons.label: Outlook raised again
reasons.text: 2026 profit guidance lifted to $13.95–$13.99 from $13.76–$13.96, and the dividend rises 5.2%.

reasons.label: Revenue beat estimates
reasons.text: Sales of $17.4B (up 10.3%) topped the roughly $17.3B analysts expected.

reasons.label: Immunology drugs surging
reasons.text: Skyrizi grew 22.7% and Rinvoq 23.9%, more than offsetting Humira's 31% decline.
